sentence: Der Forscher sagte, dass die Studentin den schwierigen Bericht gelesen hat.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix predicate selects the dass-clause as its propositional complement and assigns its external argument to Der Forscher in Spec-IP. This analysis uses the classical GB option of base-generating external subjects in Spec-IP, rather than deriving them from VP-internal positions. German VP and IP are head-final: the matrix complement precedes sagte in VP, and the matrix inflectional position follows VP. The initially empty matrix C will host the finite verb in the declarative V2 derivation. Within the embedded CP, overt dass occupies C, die Studentin occupies Spec-IP, and den schwierigen Bericht is the complement of participial gelesen. The finite perfect auxiliary hat is base-generated in embedded I; this analysis does not introduce a separate auxiliary VP. Determiners head DPs, and schwierigen is an AP left-adjoined to the object's N-bar, modifying Bericht. First, sagte assigns the researcher the Agent role and the embedded CP the propositional Theme role. Next, gelesen assigns the student the Agent role and the report the Theme role. Finite matrix I and embedded hat then license nominative on their respective subjects, while gelesen licenses accusative on its object. The object's determiner, adjective, and noun exhibit masculine singular accusative concord, with weak adjectival inflection after den. Finally, hat selects the participial predicate to establish the present perfect embedded construction. Matrix I carries past and third-person singular features compatible with the whole-word form sagte. No morphological decomposition of the supplied words is assumed, and punctuation is not introduced as an additional token.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the head-final base structure and the argument, case, and perfect-construction dependencies.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix verb moves from its previously represented VP-final position and adjoins to finite I. Its lower V position is now an unpronounced head trace, while the occurrence in the complex I head bears the pronunciation sagte. The head-movement relation connects that trace, the raised lexical head, and its inflectional host. This movement creates the finite I constituent that can subsequently move to C; recording this intermediate workspace makes V-to-I precede I-to-C. The matrix subject remains in Spec-IP, and the embedded clause is unchanged. In particular, dass remains in embedded C and hat remains in embedded I, so no embedded V2 movement is posited.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the matrix lexical verb from V to I.

relations.relation: Matrix nominative licensing through the finite-head chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: The complex I head established in the preceding stage moves as a unit and adjoins to the empty matrix C. Its previous I position becomes an unpronounced I trace; the moved constituent contains the overt lexical verb and the silent inflectional host. This I-to-C dependency supplies the head component of German declarative V2. Next, the lexical verb's dependency is updated to connect the C-contained verb with its original V trace, mediated by the I-head chain. Finally, matrix nominative licensing is preserved through the finite I chain: the I trace identifies the subject's case-licensing position, supported by the raised finite head. Der Forscher has not yet moved, so the present workspace intentionally has the finite verb before the in-situ subject and is not yet the input's completed surface structure.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the complex finite I head to matrix C.

relations.relation: Subject A-bar movement to the prefield

derivationStages.stageRecord: Der Forscher moves from the Spec-IP position represented in the preceding workspace to matrix Spec-CP, leaving an unpronounced DP trace. This is A-bar movement to the declarative prefield, not a second theta-position; it does not require a contrastive-topic interpretation. The movement relation connects the pronounced prefield DP and its subject-position trace. The resulting subject chain retains the Agent role and nominative case associated with its lower position, with case licensed through the finite I chain. The final matrix CP therefore places exactly one constituent before sagte in C. Its VP contains the selected dass-clause, whose overt complementizer blocks the matrix-style V2 derivation and whose head-final IP yields die Studentin den schwierigen Bericht gelesen hat. The adjective remains inside the object DP, and the embedded subject remains in Spec-IP. Reading the pronounced terminals gives exactly Der Forscher sagte dass die Studentin den schwierigen Bericht gelesen hat; the head and subject traces are silent. The completed analysis contains no anaphoric or pronominal dependency requiring an additional Binding Theory relation.
derivationStages.statement: Front the matrix subject to Spec-CP and complete the V2 sentence.
